habit_scope: Hang then tape; 1/2 in GWB common (CMHC). Fastener table from CMHC Ch21 as printed — Canadian / confirm AHJ. US Gypsum Association table Gap. 2-story light wood only.
how_it_is_done: Insulation, air barrier, and vapor have been seen (P13). Then hang. P11 may still be outside. No lag days invented.

Ceiling first, then walls. BD Room Additions (remodel-addition technique). CMHC: ceilings with the long dimension at right angles to trusses/joists (parallel if 1x4 strapped). Army FM 5-426 (technique, not local code): always start with the ceiling; joints on the center line of a stud or joist.

1/2 in is the common sheet. CMHC: 1/2 in more common; required min when supports are 24 in o.c. or when the GWB supports insulation. 3/8 in allowed on walls @ 16 in o.c. when boards perpendicular. P08: 1/2 in assumed in bracing lengths; 1/2 in under enclosed stairs. 24 in o.c. walls (P08 alt): screws-only 12 in o.c. — already filed, still a hold here.
Walls usually hung horizontally. Ends on a support, at a corner. CMHC. BD (remodel-addition): tight to the ceiling; 1/8 in at butt joints; 1/2 in gap at the floor. Keep both books.

Fasteners dimple the paper, they do not break it. CMHC: nails ringed, 2.3 mm (3/32 in) shank, 5.5 mm (7/32 in) heads; penetrate ≥20 mm (3/4 in) into wood; screws ≥15 mm (5/8 in) into wood. Single-nail: ceiling ≤7 in o.c., walls ≤8 in o.c. Double-nail: pairs 2 in apart, ≤12 in o.c. Screws usually 12 in o.c.; may go 16 in o.c. on walls when studs are ≤16 in. Bracing GWB: nails ≤8 in, screws ≤12 in (CMHC high wind/earthquake — Canadian / confirm AHJ). BD: ceiling screws ≥3/4 in into framing. Army FM 5-426 (technique): single 6–7 in ceiling / 6–8 in walls; double pairs 2–2-1/2 in at ~12 in; edge 3/8–1/2 in; do not double-nail the perimeter. Do not mix Army onto the CMHC table as the job schedule. US Gypsum Association table: Gap.

Float the ceiling at interior partitions so truss uplift does not crack the joint. AF&PA: unattached at least 18 in from the ceiling/wall when trusses run perpendicular to the partition (Fig 73). HUD: 16–24 in; 2x blocking as a backer; do not screw the ceiling to that blocking. Clips / hat channel CLASS. Keep 18 in vs 16–24 in.

Tape: compound, tape, cover, fold inside corners. CMHC Fig 165. ≥10°C (50°F). Fill joints >3 mm (1/8 in) first. Three coats: 125 mm (5 in) with tape; then 200 mm (8 in) recessed / 250 mm (10 in) unrecessed; then 250–300 mm (10–12 in) recessed / 400 mm (16 in) unrecessed. Nail/screw heads two coats. Nail pops: paper broken or fastener too proud / too long; lumber ≤19% MC is NBC Canadian. Fasteners just long enough cut popping (Ch21). BD (remodel-addition): 6 in knife, embed tape.
tools_equipment: Named: screw gun; trowel / wide-blade putty knife; corner bead. Army also names 4/6/12 in knives (technique). Not a SKU list.
inspection_hold_points: 1/2 in when the board supports insulation or at 24 in OC (Ch21). 1/2 in under enclosed stairs already P08.
Nail 3/4 in into wood; screw 5/8 in into wood. Dimple, paper intact.
Float 18 in (AF&PA) or 16–24 in (HUD) at partition — do not screw to the backer.
typical_duration_sfr: unknown — not in sources as a drywall-only cycle. No lag days invented.
when_this_beats_habit: This is the sourced habit/hold sequence from the phase extract.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Hanging before the insulation inspection. Breaking the paper. Fastening the ceiling into the partition backer in the float zone. Inventing IRC R-numbers or a US Gypsum Association table.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They hang rock. What they skip is 3/4 in nail penetration, dimple without breaking paper, the float zone, and tape at 50°F.
permit_gate: fire/wet-area board on drawings where required
permit_gate_notes: Canadian names stay Canadian / confirm AHJ. Not a stamp. Do not invent IRC R-numbers.
plain_language_summary: Hang 1/2-inch rock, ceilings first across the joists, walls often sideways. Ring nails 3/4 inch into the wood, or screws 5/8 inch. Dimple, do not blow the paper. Single 7/8 or double pairs at 12. Float the ceiling 18 in (AF&PA) or 16–24 in (HUD) at partitions. Tape three coats, not below 50°F.
spanish_summary: Cuelgue roca de 1/2, techos primero a traves de los joists. Clavos de anillo 3/4 en la madera, o tornillos 5/8. Dimple, no rompa el papel. Flote el techo 18 in o 16–24 in en tabiques. Cinta a tres capas, no bajo 50°F.

confidence_notes: Nail/screw penetration and OC printed in CMHC Ch21. Canadian NBC labeled. AF&PA 18 in and HUD 16–24 in float kept as variants. US Gypsum Association table still Gap.
inspector_looks_for: 1/2 in common / bracing / stairs; ceiling first; long way across joists.
Fasteners dimpled not broken; nail ≥3/4 in / screw ≥5/8 in into wood.
Single 7 in ceiling / 8 in wall or double pairs 2 in at 12 (CMHC — confirm AHJ).
Float 18 in (AF&PA) or 16–24 in (HUD) at partition; do not screw the ceiling to that backer.
24 in o.c. walls still 12 in screw if that is the filed P08 alt; tape on joints at ≥50°F.
common_messups: Nail / screw popping (CMHC; Army FM 5-426): paper broken, fastener too proud, or fastener longer than needed; lumber wetter than 19% MC (NBC Canadian / confirm AHJ).
do_not_cheap: Insulation inspection before hang (Ch2). No skip-inspection.
1/2 in where P08 bracing assumed it (hold + layering); 1/2 in under enclosed stairs (already SOP).
Do not fasten the ceiling into the partition backer in the float zone.
Do not glue this to a BWP story — wall-sheathing glue ban stays P08.
smart_save: Use fasteners just long enough to cut popping (Ch21). No dollars.
Horizontal vs vertical hang is CMHC/BD preference, not a fastener skip. Float ceiling is a callback save, not a drywall-count save.
sop_gap_note: inspector_fails unsourced. Canadian NBC. 19% MC is NBC not IRC. US Gypsum Association table Gap. Crew and pennies Gap.
